Everyone Was Watching Mom

Black Bear Cub · Great Smoky Mountains National Park, USA

This was my very first time in the Smoky Mountains, and the very first national park I had ever visited in America. I had always heard about black bears, and I was so excited just to see my first one. I had no idea that by the end of the day, I would be photographing cubs, and not just one, but pairs of them.

It started with their mother. She was grazing out in front of us, and every photographer there had their camera pointed at her. Nobody was looking anywhere else.

Nobody, that is, except my boyfriend. He is a good hunter, and he knew something the others didn't. He told me right away that if the mother was here, her cubs would be somewhere close by, most likely up in the trees.

So the two of us started searching. And there, in the tree right next to the mama bear, we saw them: two little black dots, running up and down the trunk.

"There are cubs!" he shouted.

I swung my lens up into the tree, moving it through the branches until I found them. And then I got to watch something wonderful. The two cubs ran up and down the trees and played with each other, as if we weren't there at all, as if we were no threat to them in the world. Everyone else was still focused on the mother. They missed it completely.

This little one is one of the two cubs I saw that day, caught climbing up his tree while his mother grazed out front.

It is one of my favorite pictures, because these were the very first cubs I ever saw, in my very first park in America. It was something I had always heard about, and now I had seen it for myself.

And I have to admit, it made my brother incredibly jealous. He is a wildlife photographer too.

Photographer

Vasuki Jayaweera
